messages:
alex.support: @customer_jen hi — saw your ticket SUP-11432. You said you started getting 429s after swapping to the new API key mapping this morning? Can you paste the request-ID/response headers you saw?
customer_jen: Yep. Getting them from a single service. Sample response: 

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 16 Jan 2024 18:12:03 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: rq_01F2Y3Z4
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1673886723
X-RateLimit-Scope: org

Also: our infra team rotated out nodes a few minutes earlier so outbound NAT IPs changed.
alex.support: thanks — that X-RateLimit-Scope: org is interesting. Are you sure you weren't hitting a project-level limit before and now it's the org?
customer_jen: we never saw org-scope before. flow was ok for 3 days then spike. We did a config change to apply a new API key per service group. Might have duplicated headers during rollout.
sre_zoe: quick hypothesis: if requests start hitting different NAT IPs while carrying the same API key, the system may be attributing some traffic by IP in addition to key. We have an IP affinity heuristic for soft-burst handling. If your key moved from an IP with cached quota to a new IP, you might see org fallback.
eng_infra: can you confirm whether clients send both Authorization: Bearer <token> and x-api-key? If both are present we currently favor bearer for quota attribution (per recent change). That can make it look like a different auth path kicks in mid-rollout.
customer_jen: we do send both for backward compat. Didn’t realize fallback changed.
alex.support: can you run this quick repro and paste output?
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXXX" -H "x-api-key: grp-abc" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```

customer_jen: output shows X-RateLimit-Scope: project when hitting node A, X-RateLimit-Scope: org when hitting node B. Same headers otherwise.
tier2_marc: that's consistent with a race in auth precedence + NAT rotation. Two things to check: 1) whether the bearer token is associated with a different org/project mapping, 2) whether the NAT IPs have active per-IP buckets that are being consumed by other workloads.
eng_infra: also check that your proxy isn't rewriting or stripping x-forwarded-for. For per-IP scoping we look at egress IP unless X-Forwarded-For is present and trusted.
customer_jen: our k8s egress uses a node pool with ephemeral IPs; they rotated to new IPs at 17:58. We saw first 429s right after.
sre_zoe: two likely contributors then: ephemeral IP change + dual-auth headers. When the rotation hit, requests switched to attribution path that triggered an org-level hard limit because the bearer token is scoped to the org.
quota-bot: [automated] Customer has used 102% of org hard quota for generation.tokens in the last 60s window. Current org limit: 1,000,000 tokens/min. Project buckets show 60% usage.
alex.support: thanks @quota-bot — that implies a hard org ceiling was reached while some requests still attributed to different project buckets.
tier2_marc: suggested immediate mitigations: 1) Ask customer to stop dual headers—send single x-api-key only for now so attribution stays consistent. 2) Request temporary org softburst increase or emergency override from billing for 30m. 3) Move to a dedicated egress IP or reserve a static NAT IP so attribution is consistent.
customer_jen: can you explain why project buckets didn't protect us? I thought project-level quotas would be enforced first.
sre_zoe: short answer: we enforce a prioritized evaluation: API-key -> project -> org, but IP-based soft-burst buckets sit outside that chain for short-term smoothing. Also if the auth header changes midstream we can fall back to different evaluation path. There was a recent change to favor bearer tokens when present which altered ordering.
eng_infra: added context: when a request arrives we compute attribution key set: {api_key, bearer_token, egress_ip}. The rate-limiter consults configured policies in order: explicit project binding (api_key), then project mapping via bearer, then org-level defaults. However soft-burst credits are tracked via IP and globally. If the IP has no cached cache-window credits, requests may consume org quota rapidly.
alex.support: repro checklist for engineering: 
- curl with both headers vs single header (x-api-key only).
- force egress IP switch (scale down/up) to reproduce NAT rotation.
- capture X-RateLimit-* headers and X-Request-ID for each attempt.
- include sample token/bind mappings (masked) so we can verify internal attribution.

customer_jen: trying now with x-api-key only. No 429s for ~90s, then one 429. X-Request-ID: rq_01F2Y3Z4-2, header shows X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, Scope: org.
tier2_marc: please upload full request logs (mask secrets). We'll check whether that single 429 correlates with another heavy tenant consuming the same org bucket.
eng_infra: I added a debug flag to allow logging of the computed attribution key in devprox for your token — please run with header X-Debug-Attribution: 1 once we confirm, and send logs.
customer_jen: done, logs attached to SUP-11432. It shows: 
- request 1: attribution -> api_key:grp-abc, ip:35.201.12.7, scope_hint: project
- request 2: attribution -> bearer:org-xyz, ip:35.201.12.7, scope_hint: org
- request 3: attribution -> api_key:grp-abc, ip:34.201.99.3, scope_hint: project
- request 4: attribution -> bearer:org-xyz, ip:34.201.99.3, scope_hint: org (429)

sre_zoe: that pattern nails it. The bearer token is mapped to the org and occasionally wins precedence, leading to org counting. When your egress IP rotates, IP-bucket/softburst behavior changes and the timing causes the org buckets to spike.
alex.support: resolution plan: 
- Short term: advise customer to send single header (x-api-key) while we roll a config that keeps api_key precedence even if bearer exists for their tenant. Also offered a temp org increase for 1hr (billing ok?).
- Mid term: engineering to add deterministic precedence config per customer and include an option to disable IP-based softburst for orgs that want strict project isolation.
eng_infra: creating ENG-8764 to add per-tenant precedence toggle + better telemetry.
tier2_marc: I'll open a billing escalation for SUP-11432 to increase org quota for 60 minutes while they stabilize.
customer_jen: thanks — we'll stop sending bearer and pin a static NAT IP. Also please confirm whether this could affect invoicing if we temporarily raise org quota.
alex.support: billing will annotate the ticket; short-term override is billed at pro-rata usage, we'll note it.
quota-bot: [automated] Org override granted until 1780016365 (60 minutes).
customer_jen: after pinning static IP and single header no 429s in last 15m. Looks resolved for now.
alex.support: great — keeping this open till ENG-8764 lands. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
